analysis.investment_thesis: B.R.Goyal is a small civil-construction contractor with decent headline numbers (P/E 8.4, ROE 14.1%, ROCE 17.9%) but operates in a capital-intensive, commoditized, government-tender-dependent industry with no durable moat. The 2025 swing to negative operating cash flow (-INR 36 Cr) and free cash flow (-INR 58 Cr) despite record profits is exactly the working-capital-absorbing pattern I avoid.
key_strengths: Revenue 5Y CAGR 15.1% and PAT 5Y CAGR 25.6% with expanding operating margins (7.5% → 8.4%)
Low debt: borrowings INR 77 Cr vs equity INR 245 Cr (D/E ~0.31)
High promoter holding at 73.60% indicates skin in the game
key_risks: 2025 OCF of -INR 36 Cr vs PAT of INR 25 Cr — earnings not translating to cash
No moat: roads/bridges contracting is tender-driven, low switching costs, fragmented
Revenue already dipped from INR 589 Cr (2024) to INR 510 Cr (2025); order-book cyclicality
red_flags: Equity nearly doubled (INR 127 → 245 Cr) in 2025 via financing inflow of INR 92 Cr — recent IPO dilution, limited public track record
Free cash flow cumulatively near zero over 6 years (~INR -3 Cr), with reported profits of INR 86 Cr
Receivables/WIP absorbing cash — classic contractor accounting risk
analysis.detailed_analysis:
The business is understandable but unattractive by my standards. Civil construction is one of the worst industries I know of — it ties up capital in receivables and retention money, competes on price for government tenders, carries execution and litigation risk, and earns returns barely above its cost of capital across a cycle. Yes, ROCE of 17.9% looks fine today, but the fact that six years of reported profits (~INR 86 Cr cumulative) have produced essentially zero cumulative free cash flow tells you where the "earnings" really live — in working capital, not shareholder pockets. The 2025 OCF of -INR 36 Cr on record PAT of INR 25 Cr confirms this.

At INR 270 Cr market cap and 8.4x earnings, the price isn't absurd, but cheapness alone never protected me from a fair business. The IPO-era capital raise (financing CF +INR 92 Cr, equity doubling) means the public-market track record is short, and the revenue dip from INR 589 Cr to INR 510 Cr suggests the growth story is lumpy. I'd rather pay a fair price for a toll-road concession with a 30-year contract than a cheap price for the contractor building it. Pass.
